title: [scan-backstop] dueSlot: characterization test for the backstop slot due on a tick
body:
Target: PeaceG03/PeaceSTOCKS

add a characterization test for dueSlot in src/scan-backstop.ts: due backstop slots
- dueSlot(new Date("2026-10-13T06:00:00Z")) is new Date("2026-10-13T05:30:00Z")
- dueSlot(new Date("2026-10-13T10:00:00Z")) is new Date("2026-10-13T09:30:00Z")
- dueSlot(new Date("2026-10-13T05:59:00Z")) is null
- dueSlot(new Date("2026-10-13T07:00:00Z")) is null
- dueSlot(new Date("2026-10-11T06:00:00Z")) is null

(Builder pre-file, TEST_CASE_EXISTING, public-test-case-existing-v3): Peace's task (source: peace). dueSlot (which slot a :47 backstop tick is responsible for: 30-89 min after 05:30Z or 09:30Z, Tue-Sat only) has no direct test, and its slot branch is never reached by the suite; this pins the window edges and the weekday rule. Production safety: test-only: one new src/*.test.ts file only: no source edits, no fix commit. Job B grades it fix-free: the test passes on the current code and fails with the function body stubbed. The running scanner chain is unchanged. A box dry-run on PeaceSTOCKS 8b1f413 (Workspace main 616c083, live 26-rule approved list, Node 22) built exactly one candidate (public-test-case-existing-v3); a local Job B run graded it COUNTS (the new test passes on the current code and fails with dueSlot stubbed); suite 574/574 with all eleven new tests of this batch, all 4 typechecks ok. Disjoint file: each task in this batch creates its own new test file. Expected COUNTS.)
